transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood CSM), Jordan Reyes (HelioCart Head of ML), Taylor Brooks (HelioCart SRE), Aisha Karim (HelioCart VP Product)

Summary:
- Quarterly review covering usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents in Q3, and alignment on roadmap and next steps for Dedicated pilot.
- Customer interested in Dedicated capacity pilot to stabilize tail latency for checkout flows; cost optimization opportunities discussed (batching, quantization).

Topics:
- Usage & spend breakdown
- Reliability incidents and SLOs
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, SSO)
- Roadmap & pilot plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll run about an hour. quick roll call?
[00:12] Jordan: yep Jordan here, aisha and taylor are on as well.
[00:17] Taylor: hey
[00:20] Maya: great, so quick agenda: usage, costs, reliability incidents, then roadmap and next steps. sound good?
[00:28] Jordan: yes
[00:30] Liam: i'll jump in on the performance bits, especially the tail latency stuff you flagged.

[02:05] Jordan: to start, our overall token usage is up about 45% q/q. checkout assistant is the big driver, especially during peak promotions. costs are creeping up and finance is asking for a plan.
[02:35] Maya: understood, we pulled the per-route token and cost dashboard. looks like the chat completion route is 68% of spend, embeddings only 14%. there are some large prompts in the checkout flow that could be cached.
[03:10] Taylor: we saw several 99th percentile spikes during the late night orders on sept 12 and sept 19; those align with autoscaler thrash and some GPU queueing.
[03:30] Liam: yeah on sept 19 there was a piq, queueing due to a burst of long sequences. we recommended enabling prefix KV caching for the checkout templates and a small increase in reserved concurrency. that dropped 95th/99th in the PoC we ran.
[04:05] Jordan: the perf improvement looked good in the report, but we're worried about costs for reserved capacity. finance asked whether Dedicated or better batching would be cheaper.
[04:30] Maya: good question. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower per-token cost for steady-state but requires commitment. for spiky traffic, a mix (dedicated baseline + hosted burst) is often best. we also recommended quantization to reduce GPU memory footprint.
[04:58] Aisha: can you remind us of the SLA differences?
[05:05] Priya: Redwood's Dedicated SLA covers availability targets and lower tail latency SLOs; hosted has best-effort for tail and region fallback policies. i'll send the SLA doc link after.

[06:20] Taylor: another ask from infra: we want to run a 48-hour dedicated benchmark with our exact workload to get unit cost numbers. can redwood run that?
[06:35] Liam: absolutely, we can stand up a dedicated pool for the bench. we'll need your traces and seq distribution, and we have a config template.
[06:50] Jordan: i'll get those over. prep: what metrics do you need specifically?
[06:58] Liam: ideally raw request traces with timestamps, token counts, seq lengths; 99th/95th latency targets; example prompt prefixes for KV caching.

[08:10] Jordan: on security, we need SOC 2 + KMS integration and SAML SSO in place. any blockers?
[08:20] Maya: we're SOC 2 Type II. KMS integrations supported across Private and Dedicated; Hosted supports customer-managed keys for some tiers. SAML SSO and RBAC supported — i'll share the compliance packet.
[08:45] Aisha: what about data residency? we need EU region hosting for payment data.
[08:52] Priya: we can pin Dedicated pools to eu-west region; private deployment option also possible for stricter controls.

[10:05] Taylor: during the spikes we saw errors referencing 'KV chash' in the logs — is that a known misspelling?
[10:12] Liam: haha yeah that's our transcription or log name mismatch, it's KV cache. we did see some stale cache keys causing extra compute; fixed by TTL tuning.

[12:00] Jordan: pricing — finance wants a clear delta between hosted incremental cost vs dedicated commit.
[12:10] Maya: we'll put together a side-by-side: per-token hosted list, dedicated committed rate, and an example with your projected q4 usage to show break-even.

[14:30] Aisha: roadmap question: any upcoming features for lower-cost embeddings?
[14:40] Liam: we're rolling an embeddings-optimized quant profile next quarter that reduces GPU cost for batch workloads. also intelligent batching improvements in Redwood Optimize will help.

[16:00] Jordan: any concerns about model drift or regressions with quantization?
[16:08] Liam: we recommend canarying quantized variants and running your eval prompt set. Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to evals; we'll help set that up for the checkout intents.

[20:20] Taylor: operationally, what about tracing and observability? we need token-level cost breakdowns per route and per-model latencies.
[20:32] Priya: Console has per-route dashboards, traces and traces hooks; we can also set up alerts for cost anomalies and latency regressions.

[25:00] Jordan: okay concretely let's outline the pilot: 1) 48-hour dedicated benchmark with HelioCart workload; 2) show cost comparison and break-even; 3) SOC2/SAML/KMS docs and region pinning confirmation; 4) follow-up exec summary.
[25:20] Maya: yes, and we'll include batching + KV cache recommendations and an estimate on token savings if applied.

[30:00] Action items recap:
- Maya: Send updated pricing & Dedicated proposal (include hosted burst options)
- Liam: Schedule and run 48-hour benchmark; share config template
- Taylor: Provide traces, seq distributions, 99th percentile targets
- Priya: Share onboarding checklist, SLA and SOC2 docs

[32:10] Jordan: timeline we have internal budget review week of oct 12, decision point around oct 20.
[32:20] Maya: we'll aim to get the benchmark results and pricing in advance of that.

[40:00] Aisha: small note — are there any known limitations with our LLM stack that would block checkout personalization? we use long context windows sometimes.
[40:12] Liam: long contexts add cost; we can use prefix KV caching to fold the fixed parts of the conversation and only send deltas. that reduces per-request tokens. also model distillation/shorter context models may help for some intents.

[50:00] Priya: i'll follow up with the links: SLA doc, SOC2 packet, onboarding playbook, and dedicated proposal draft.
[50:20] Maya: thanks everyone.
[50:25] Jordan: thanks all

[59:30] End of call

References and Links Mentioned:
- Benchmark config template (to be shared)
- SLA and SOC2 packet (Priya to send)
- Onboarding checklist/playbook (Priya)

Notes on Transcription Quality: medium — some product names and acronyms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., KV chash -> KV cache, "piq" -> "peak"), filler words and overlaps present.
